primary_sources.evidence: French Ministry of Culture archaeological account describes round and horseshoe towers emerging from a monumental talus on the southern and western fronts.
The central core is protected at its southern and western base by a monumental glacis containing defensive galleries.
UNESCO identifies the fortress hilltop/ridge setting; these landscape relationships are preserved.

contact_evidence.method: Source geometry foot edges compared against corrected production ground; exact replacement toe positions were then independently sampled. Raised gallery roof/floor remains intentional; its load-bearing lower wall skin now reaches ground.

geometry_invariants.outer_wall: Original centreline subdivisions, base references and crowns retained. Only battered lower edge heights extend into sampled terrain.
geometry_invariants.talus: Original crown elevation15.22607421875m and crown width6m retained. Each lower edge splays4.8m, the existing intended architectural estimate; explicit keyword arguments keep batter distinct from merlon visibility. Bottom faces extend to measured ground minus0.5m.
geometry_invariants.towers: Mapped eight tower prisms and the three southern round towers retain their original upper geometry. Added perimeter skins continue their existing lower outlines to ground.
geometry_invariants.courtyard: Mapped inner courtyard remains open except the narrow western loggia walkway supporting its existing arches; gallery roof tessellation is unchanged.
geometry_invariants.terrain: No landscape flattening or new terrain cut; no lowering of castle datum. Foundation embedding is0.5m below terrain at each toe.
geometry_invariants.loggia: A 3m wide, 39.6m long stone walkway beneath the existing western arch line has terrain-fitted retaining sides and a thin paving cap at the original arch floor. Its secondary dimensions follow the authored arch footprint, not an archaeological survey.

quantitative_ground.coverage: All wall and tower support query positions from LOD0,LOD1 andLOD2; generator verifies that no queried position is absent.

limitations: The production DEM resolves terrain at metre-scale sampling but smooths historic scarps. Precise buried foundation depths, mortar profiles and the4.8m talus splay remain secondary architectural estimates; the record does not present them as archaeological measurements.
